key_insight: Ultra-high-precision LEED, STM, and DFT show that oxygen on Rh(100) has a previously misidentified 0.50 ML ground state made of nano-domains, while the 0.25 ML phase features fourfold hollow adsorption with second-layer buckling.
engineering_relevance: These corrected atomic-scale structures refine surface chemistry models for Rh catalysts and improve how ordered/disordered adsorbate phases are interpreted in diffraction-based surface characterization.
method: Quantitative LEED structure refinement with ultra-low Pendry R factors (~0.07)
Variable-temperature STM to probe ordering and nano-domain behavior
DFT plus short-range order simulations to test candidate surface models and diffraction extinction
evidence_signal: The paper reports single-digit picometer structural precision from LEED and uses short-range order simulations to explain why nano-domain scattering suppresses expected diffraction spots.
watch_item: The 0.50 ML phase is highly temperature-sensitive and domain-rich, so experimental interpretation depends strongly on disorder and coherent domain averaging.
paper_title: Oxygen on Rh(100) revisited with ultra-high precision
